_comment: Guided tour of the VV/VH anisotropy tool. Steps point at real controls; the ones the user must use wait for them.

steps.title: Load a VV/VH file
steps.text: The file holds the parallel decay (VV) followed by the perpendicular decay (VH). Press Load VV/VH file… (or drop the file on the window). Both decays and r(t) appear at once.

await.hint: Press Load VV/VH file… and choose a .dat or .txt file.

steps.title: Set the G-factor
steps.text: r(t) = (VV - g VH) / (VV + 2 g VH). The G-factor corrects the different sensitivity of the two detection channels; a wrong g tilts the whole curve, so take it from a reference measurement.

await.hint: Change G-factor and press Enter; watch r(t) and r∞ move.

steps.title: Subtract the backgrounds
steps.text: Constant backgrounds are subtracted from VV and VH before r(t) is formed. Points where the denominator is not positive are left out of r(t).

steps.title: Choose the r∞ region
steps.text: r∞ is the mean of r(t) over the region between the two green lines. Drag the lines in the plot, or type the bounds. Pick a stretch where r(t) has levelled off and the noise is still small.

steps.title: Read r∞
steps.text: Five decimals; N/A when no valid point lies in the region.

steps.title: Save the results
steps.text: Writes three files next to the name you choose: the shifted decays, the anisotropy trace (channel, r(t), r(t) minus r∞) and the r∞ metadata.

await.hint: Press Save outputs… and choose a name.

steps.title: Process many files
steps.text: The batch window computes r∞ for every queued file with the settings that are current when it opens.
